notes.title: Summer Update & Gamescom
notes.content:
[p]Hello everyone![/p][p][/p][p]We have just returned to our desks from our summer holidays, and work continues on our less than summery game. [/p][p][/p][p]Since our reveal in the spring, a lot of things have fallen into place with Frostrail, and we are eager to show you more of them a little later. Over the past months, the combat gameplay in particular has improved by leaps and bounds. We’ve spent a lot of time honing the feel of combat, adjusting animations, sounds and enemy mechanics to find the perfect mix of fantasy and realism. The Revenants are really angry now! We’ll write more about these enemies soon.[/p][p][/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45577624/93070d7bbfecc1b0b4a9b6d9fd2e4f4fb9fa64d7.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45577624/7a193542ff87ced5286b873659cc1cc7ee0ccb21.jpg"][/img][/carousel][p]Another part of the game that has received a lot of attention recently are the visuals. Our art team has been hard at work creating a whole bunch of new assets like buildings, trees and everyday items. This has really improved the overall style and all the small details, and helped us home in on the atmosphere of desolation. We also have new weapon models to complement the combat improvements, and to help you stay alive in the harsh environment.[/p][p][/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45577624/afa2a8d4364c9e22d6ac22564b8bebd10bbd3e06.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45577624/8067cb6d85a991a7f74663a4366e2bd266346342.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45577624/d59ff61c0360f2ab9af27798f470251fb397febf.png"][/img][/carousel][p]Additionally, we’ve revised the way we build locations in the world. Earlier in the development process, locations were largely built from premade assets by level designers. In other words, artists would create the building blocks, and level designers would make the levels with them.[/p][p][/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45577624/bf242d3203ab68063fe407c1776a45ecc5ab41ca.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45577624/c94cd226b3fe91996ea87f56c1df487cfb9bdd65.png"][/img][/carousel][p]This is still how it works with much of the world, but we’ve shifted our workflow a bit and had artists work more directly on key locations. This has allowed us to make the points of interest look a lot better, with more hand-drawn and hand-placed structures and clutter in them. We look forward to hearing what you think about the look and feel of exploration![/p][p][/p][p]Next up for our team is preparing for a visit to Gamescom in Cologne, Germany. Keep your eyes peeled – there might be video snippets coming your way from the trip![/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Frequently Asked Questions about Frostrail
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45577624/7580bfa45546f90ca3b4ea19a8202308368f47f9.png[/img]

Hello everyone!

Now that we’ve had a couple of weeks to read through your comments and questions, we wanted to reply to a few of the most frequently asked ones. Have a read below, and post in the comments here or on [url=https://discord.gg/KtXN6eQfs3]Discord[/url] if you have anything else on your mind that you’d like to know.

[h3]Frostrail FAQ[/h3]

[b]When is Frostrail releasing?[/b]

Frostrail is planned to be released into Early Access on Steam in 2026.

[b]Will there be a public playtest?[/b]

Ideally yes. Right now the plan is to have multiple closed test sessions before Early Access, and if our schedule allows, a larger public playtest as well. We’ll keep you posted!

[b]What engine does the game use?[/b]

Frostrail is developed on Unreal Engine 5.

[b]How much will it cost?[/b]

It is still too early to give any exact numbers, and we want to avoid making any guesses to prevent misinterpretation and confusion. The price will only be finalized as we release on Steam.

[b]How many people can you play with?[/b]

Frostrail has been developed with crews of 1–4 players in mind. This is an aspect we will continue to evaluate during development and Early Access to find a good balance between crew size and challenge.

[b]Is the game going to be moddable?[/b]

Unfortunately, due partially to the constraints of the game engine, full moddability of the kind we have with Barotrauma is not a possibility with this game. However, we will explore other avenues for customizability and even smaller-scale modding support during development and Early Access.

[b]Is Frostrail made by the same people as Barotrauma?[/b]

Yes! The Frostrail team includes many FakeFish developers who have worked on Barotrauma, as well as new talents hired specifically for Frostrail.

[b]Will Frostrail have controller support?[/b]

Controller support is in the development plans, but it will probably not be available immediately at the start of Early Access. We will keep you posted.

[b]Will Frostrail release on consoles?[/b]

Frostrail will be released first in Early Access on PC-Steam. We will evaluate possible console ports for 1.0 and beyond.

[b]Will Frostrail be MacOs/Linux compatible?[/b]

One of our developers is primarily working on Linux, and we are eager to open Frostrail to the Linux gaming community. So that’s a tentative yes at this point at least for Linux. Our number one priority is making the PC version smooth and stable for Early Access release, and Linux/Mac support is also kept in mind every step of the way. However, we can only fully confirm support for these OS upon release.

[b]Are you looking for marketing partnerships?[/b]

Shiro Unlimited, the publisher for Frostrail, handles the game’s marketing through their own trusted partners, so at this time we at FakeFish are not looking to enter into new marketing partnerships.

[b]Can I translate the game for you into my language?[/b]

Like marketing, the game localization process is being handled entirely by our publisher Shiro, so we’re not looking to source translations from elsewhere at the moment.

notes.title: Meet the team behind Frostrail
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45577624/be937dc80aa950897cd60beafa2f9aeaf66c772c.png[/img]

Hello everyone!

We’ve been thrilled to see so much interest in Frostrail since last week’s announcement. Thank you for all the questions and comments, and keep them coming – we’re looking forward to hearing what you think, and will be writing to answer as many questions as we can in the coming weeks and months.

This week we wanted to help you get to know us a little better: You may have heard of FakeFish before, but what kind of people are there behind the name? Those who have been following us for a longer time through Barotrauma already know something about our team, but there are developers behind Frostrail who have not worked on Barotrauma, and vice versa. So we believe some introductions are in order.

[h3]FakeFish, the makers of Frostrail and Barotrauma[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45577624/5848929d08753e31c72ff9af37a4a0f4d21a7d66.png[/img]
[i]A picture from a few years back with almost half of the current team.[/i]

FakeFish is an independent game studio from Turku, Finland. Our journey started all the way back in 2014, when the team consisted of five university friends, but we only really made our mark when Barotrauma was released on Steam early access in 2019.

That same year was also when the idea for Frostrail began to take shape: it started as our lead designer Ez’s brainchild when he was traveling to his summer cottage along a particularly foggy and deserted highway through the forest, and daydreamed: "Wouldn't it be cool if there was some sort of truck simulator meets Silent Hill or something?". The daydream lingered, changing shape bit by bit and morphing from a truck game into a train game over the years, until the opportunity came to develop it further with a team.

Now that team is almost 30 strong – still a small company, but just about big enough to handle two separate game projects. Our people come from 8 different countries (most of us are Finnish though), and some have called FakeFish home for the entirety of their careers, while others have experience from several different video game companies. The Fish currently working on Frostrail are…

[b]Design team[/b]
Ez, Daniel, Jeroen and Riina

[b]Art team[/b]
Jonas, Dinh, Iiro, Mappu, Nam-Anh, Sampo and Tomi

[b]Programming team[/b]
Sami, Eetu, Jaakko, Juan, Kasperi and Lauri

[b]Audio and music[/b]
Jussi

[b]Production and community management[/b]
Aku, Kalle and Vilma


You can find almost everyone from FakeFish in the [url=https://discord.gg/KtXN6eQfs3]official Discord server[/url], albeit with our Discord nicknames, as well as members of the publishing team at Shiro. Come say hi!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45577624/a3fb21d835aa3c5f473c01ff879d787e9124719e.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Welcome to Frostrail, a journey through the cold
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=x_59w8EP9Qs;full][/previewyoutube]

Greetings wayfarer, and welcome on board.

You’ve just taken your first step on the journey called Frostrail, and we’re thrilled to have you with us! Let’s talk a little bit about this game that we at FakeFish and Shiro Games have been working on for a couple of years already, behind the scenes.

Frostrail is the upcoming second game of FakeFish, the Finnish game studio behind the submarine simulator [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/602960/Barotrauma/]Barotrauma[/url]. Frostrail is an entirely new survival horror adventure through the cold and dark – not an alien ocean, but a post-apocalyptic world of ice and eldritch enemies. The second half of the team behind Frostrail is the French publisher Shiro Unlimited, the third party publishing arm of Shiro Games, known for the multi-million-selling RTS Northgard, the critically acclaimed turn-based RPG Wartales, and the recently announced online space exploration and building game SpaceCraft.

For our very first post, we wanted to introduce you to the world of Frostrail. Namely, what is the game all about, and what will it be like to play it?

[h3]The cold ashes of a fallen empire[/h3]
Imagine a place on Earth where nearly all life has been bled dry, frozen over and disfigured by a malevolent force at the behest of a warmongering religious zealot. Then imagine you are one of the few people who have so far managed to avoid that fate. You face unfavorable odds with very little by way of arms or resources, but you do have one thing going for you: a train.

Frostrail centers around an armored, steam-powered train, your lifeline and moving base. Traverse the frozen wastes in pursuit of salvation somewhere beyond the northern horizon, and don’t stray too far from your train: it’s your only reliable source of heat, and you don’t want the cold to catch you.

[h3]Dieselpunk FPS survival crafting game[/h3]
Frostrail is a first-person shooter where ammo is a luxury and fights are nothing to be taken lightly. Besides fighting, or trying to avoid unnecessary fights, you’ll explore the ruins of a former empire, gather supplies, craft clothes, food and weapons. Crucially, you’ll upgrade, maintain and operate your train, and its life-sustaining Eden Engine.

You play as one (or up to four, if you bring friends!) of very few survivors in a disaster-torn world, and along the way you will be challenged by a multitude of enemies known as Revenants. Revenants are connected to and have been twisted by the same entity that is responsible for the persistent cold. Revenants, despite their gruesome shapes and the significant threat they pose, are the cannon fodder enemy – there are worse things to come, later.

[h3] Coming to Steam in 2026[/h3]
Frostrail will begin its Early Access journey on Steam next year, and there is much we’re eager to tell you about the game even before that: stay tuned for playtests, feature sneak peeks, and more in the months to come. Be sure to follow and add Frostrail to your wishlist on Steam to stay up to speed with our news!

If you’d like to meet other travelers as well as the people behind Frostrail, you can now join us on the official Discord server. Click the invite link below, and see you on the other side.
